skills.name: Use the discriminant to decide the nature of the roots

note.text:
For ax² + bx + c = 0 the discriminant is D = b² − 4ac.
• D > 0: two different real roots; the parabola crosses the x-axis twice.
• D = 0: one repeated (equal) root; the parabola touches the x-axis at its turning point.
• D < 0: no real roots; the parabola does not meet the x-axis.
If D is a perfect square, the roots are rational and the quadratic factorises.
Unknown coefficients: equal roots means D = 0; real roots means D ≥ 0.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text:
By the end, you should be able to use D = b² − {4}ac to say whether a quadratic equation has two, one or no real roots, and find unknown coefficients from that.
Builds on: Lesson {9} (the quadratic formula) and Lesson {23} (parabolas).
Leads to: Lesson {25} (solving with graphs) and, in Form Five, intersections of lines and curves.

sections.heading: Why the discriminant decides
sections.text:
In x = (−b ± √D)/{2}a, the number D = b² − {4}ac sits under the square root.
• D positive: √D is a real number, and ± gives two different roots.
• D = {0}: ±{0} changes nothing: one repeated root.
• D negative: there is no real square root: no real roots.
On the graph of y = ax² + bx + c these are: crosses the x-axis twice, touches it, misses it.
Example: {quad(1, -6, 9)}: D = {36} − {36} = {0}, one root x = {3}.

sections.heading: Finding unknowns
sections.text:
• Equal roots: x² + kx + {9} = {0}: D = k² − {36} = {0}, so k = {6} or {-6}.
• Real roots: x² + {mono(4, 'x')} + k = {0}: D = {16} − {4}k ≥ {0}, so k ≤ {4}.
• No real roots: use D < {0}.
When D is a perfect square ({1}, {4}, {9}, …), the roots are rational and the quadratic factorises.

mistake.why: √{0} = {0}, so the formula gives x = −b/{2}a: one root, counted twice.

worked_example.problem: Find the positive value of k for which x² + kx + {m * m} = {0} has equal roots.
steps: Equal roots means D = {0}: a = {1}, b = k, c = {m * m}.
k = {2 * m} or k = {-2 * m}. Check: x² + {mono(2 * m, 'x')} + {m * m} = (x + {m})², one repeated root.

cards.idea: The sign of D = b² − {4}ac decides how many real roots there are.
example: D > {0}: two; D = {0}: one (equal); D < {0}: none

cards.idea: On the graph: D > {0} crosses the x-axis twice, D = {0} touches it, D < {0} misses it.
example: y = {quad(1, 0, 4)}: D = {-16} < {0}, the curve stays above the x-axis

cards.idea: Equal roots: set D = {0} and solve for the unknown.
example: x² + kx + {9} = {0} has equal roots when k² = {36}: k = {6} or {-6}

check.prompt: Find the positive value of k for which x² + kx + {m * m} = {0} has equal roots.

misconceptions.explain: That is k². Take the square root: k = {2 * m}.

questions.prompt: Describe the roots of {quad(a, b, c)} = {0}.
questions.correct: {b * b - 4 * a * c > 0 ? 'Two different real roots' : b * b - 4 * a * c == 0 ? 'Two equal real roots (one repeated root)' : 'No real roots'}

distractors.text: {b * b - 4 * a * c > 0 ? 'No real roots' : 'Two different real roots'}
{b * b - 4 * a * c == 0 ? 'No real roots' : 'Two equal real roots (one repeated root)'}

misconceptions.explain: Work out D = {b * b - 4 * a * c} and look at its sign.
D = {b * b - 4 * a * c}: equal roots need D = {0} exactly.
A quadratic has at most two roots.

questions.prompt: How many times does the graph of y = {quad(a, b, c)} meet the x-axis?
questions.correct: {b * b - 4 * a * c > 0 ? 'Twice' : b * b - 4 * a * c == 0 ? 'Once (it touches the axis)' : 'Never'}

distractors.text: {b * b - 4 * a * c == 0 ? 'Twice' : 'Once (it touches the axis)'}

misconceptions.explain: Look at the sign of D = {b * b - 4 * a * c}.
Touching needs D = {0}; here D = {b * b - 4 * a * c}.
A parabola meets a straight line at most twice.

solution: The number of crossings is the number of real roots of {quad(a, b, c)} = {0}.

questions.prompt: Find the positive value of k for which x² + kx + {m * m} = {0} has equal roots.

misconceptions.explain: That is k². Take the square root: k = {2 * m}.

questions.prompt: For which values of k does x² + {mono(2 * h, 'x')} + k = {0} have real roots?

misconceptions.explain: D = {4 * h * h} − {4}k ≥ {0} gives k ≤ {h * h}: larger k makes D negative.
Equal roots (D = {0}) are real too, so k = {h * h} is allowed.
Square the coefficient of x: ({2 * h})² = {4 * h * h}.

questions.prompt: Find k if kx² + {mono(b, 'x')} + {1} = {0} has equal roots.

misconceptions.explain: D = b² − {4}ac with a = k: {b * b} − {4}k = {0}, so k = {b * b / 4}.
